MMI-NST Manual 2.3

Overview:

    Micro Magic's New SpiceTool (NST for short) is a utility program for viewing waveforms generated by programs like HSPICE. NST can read HSPICE binary format files (9007, 9601 formats) and ASCII columnated files. NST was designed to work with schematic front-end programs such as Micro Magic's SUE. In this mode, highlighted nets on a schematic can be cross-probed easily. Furthermore, the schematic program automatically determines the hierarchical net names associated with the net which is often times difficult to determine. Nevertheless, NST can be used in a stand-alone mode if desired.

    Key features provided by NST:

    • Very fast even up to very large dataset sizes (>100 MB). No known size limitation in either nodes or timesteps.

    • Multiple voltage and/or current panels

    • Accepts multiple spice output files concurrently

    • reads binary tr0, sw0, and ac0, and ASCII columnated files.

    • Can read partial binary files.

    • Ability to derive nodes as arbitrary arithmetic expressions of existing nodes.

    • Selectable X axis (defaults to time in .tr0 files)

    • Graphical user interface

    • Postscript output of screen

    • Log or linear axes

    • Bi-endian support (thanks to Stefanos Sidiropoulos)

Running NST:

    To run NST standalone, you can type: 

    	nst <switches> <data_filename>
    where <switches> can include zero or more of "-geometry <X-geometry>" or "-display <X-display>". All switches must precede any data files. Note that nst must be in your search path.

    The file ${MMI_TOOLS}/nst/.nstrc contains all the user-modifiable options in NST. After ${MMI_TOOLS}/nst/.nstrc is sourced, NST will attempt to source ~/.nstrc. Finally, NST will attempt to source ./.nstrc (i.e. from the current directory) for any directory specific customizations. Thus any individual users who have preferences for certain NST defaults can copy those parts of the .nstrc file into their home directory and/or schematic directories and make whatever modifications they so desire. Consult ${MMI_TOOLS}/nst/.nstrc for what customizations are available.

NST Operation:

    NST displays a message in the status bar (just to the right of the menu items like File, View, etc. The default value for the status bar is the title card of the most recently loaded waveform. When you move the mouse over the various entries in the menus or the names of signals in the legend, the status bar will change to provide additional documentation about what you can do if you click the buttons where you are.

    Loading a file:

    Click on the "File" button to display a file menu. Click on "Load..." to load in a new data file. A popup window will be created where you can type in the file name followed by <Return> or clicking "Done". If the file is correctly loaded, the window title will be changed to include the file name and the title card of the file will be displayed in the banner. The file name will also be added to the "File" pulldown menu.

    Since multiple files can be loaded with this mechanism, NST sometimes must choose which file to use on certain operations, (e.g. deriving new nodes). If there is an ambiguity, NST will always use the most recently loaded file.

    Note that reloading a file is the accepted way of dealing with new simulation data -- one need not exit and reenter NST. While individual data sets cannot be unloaded from NST, all datasets can be unloaded with the "Reset" command in the "File" menu which will place NST in its initialized state.

    Displaying a waveform:

    Once the desired file is loaded, a listbox of nodes can be created by clicking on the "File" button and then clicking on the file name. Double-clicking on the desired node in the listbox will then display it in the selected panel. Alternatively the plot and unplot buttons can be used to plot the selected node. Note that currents are prefixed by "I(" and will display in separate panels to voltages. The "Close" button will delete the node listbox but not otherwise affect NST.

    Waveforms are plotted from a list of colors defined in the .nstrc file using a line like: 

    		set NST_COLORS {green yellow pink red lightblue}

    After every plot, the current color is indexed thus, with the default colors, you can cycle through 5 colors.

    If you have multiple waveforms with the same color, you can move the cursor over the waveform's name in the legend which will change that layer's color to white as long as the cursor stays over that entry in the legend.

    You can also move waveforms to different panels by clicking and holding down button one (the left button) over its entry in the legend, moving the cursor to the desired window, and then releasing the button. You can not put voltages in current panels or visa versa. Also, you must release the button in the panel over the waveform display, not over any margins.

    You can also unplot or change the color of a signal by holding down button-2 (the middle button) over its entry in the legend and then choosing either "unplot" or the desired color in the popup menu.

    NOTE that if you cannot read the entries in the legend (the list of currently plotted waveforms in the upper right corner of each graph), move the mouse over the legend to raise it. If it is still obscured, click on the "<" or ">" at the right edge of the menu bar to increase or decrease the right margin of the graph to make more room for the legend.

    Clicking on "Erase All Panels" in the "View" menu will erase all panels and reset the window to show only one panel. Note that this function does not unload data.

    Zooming and Measuring

    The three mouse buttons are used for zooming and measuring in panels. The mouse position in spice units is shown in the lower left had part of the window and the most recent measurement is shown in the lower right hand part of the window. The mouse buttons have the following functions: 

    		<Button-1>	drags a zoom box over a panel
		<Button-2>	drags a measure box over a panel
		<Button-3>	zooms to fit all waveforms

    The menu command "Zoom to Last" with hotkey "z" returns to the last view.

    The menu command "Zoom to..." brings up a popup form which you can specify the coords of the window to zoom to. This is particularly handy when you have multiple panels up and you want each panel to have the same Y (typically voltage) limits for comparison. In this case, set the "All Panels" binary indicator in the popup. Otherwise, the Y limits are autoscaled to the waveforms in each panel and will likely be different.

    Commonly, you want to measure the delay between two voltage waveforms at the mid-supply crossing. While this can be approximated using the "measure box", an alternative command exists. 

    		<Shift-Button-2>	measure between fixed y-coordinate

    To measure, press button-2 while holding down the shift key. Move the button near a waveform and an "X" will appear to mark the starting position of the waveform. This "X" will be located at the defined y-coordinate as discussed next. While still holding down button-2, move the mouse to another waveform and an annotated horizontal line will show the x distance between the waveforms. You can move the mouse to another point to move the endpoint of the measurement but you have to release button-2 and press it again to change the reference point.

    The default y-coordinate for this measure command is defined in the .nstrc file by the line: 

    		set MEASURE_YCOORD <vector|number>

    You can set this either to a plotting entity (waveform), either derived or loaded, in which case the y value of the first point in that waveform will be used. Alternatively, you can set it to a value, like 1.125.

    To set the y-coordinate while in NST, use the "Change Measure Y Coordinate" command in the "Misc" menu. This will prompt you for a new value. If the y-coord is not valid when commencing a measure, this command will also be executed automatically to let you fix it.

    Managing the Panels:

    NST permits any number of voltage and/or current panels, limited only by the screen resolution. NST uses the concept of a "selected" panel into which all plotting/unplotting is done. The border of the selected panel is highlighted. A different panel can be selected by clicking any mouse button on the desired panel.

    NST will not mix voltage and current waveforms, i.e. they must be in separate panels. When plotting, NST will try to plot in the selected panel. If it finds that the selected panel is a different type than the node to be plotting (e.g. a current panel and a voltage node) then it will try to find a panel of the correct type to select and display the waveform in. If none exists, then a new panel will be created, selected, and the waveform will be displayed there.

    A new panel can be added by clicking on "Add Panel" in the "View" menu and the selected panel can be removed by clicking on "Remove Selected Panel" in the "View" menu.

    During zooming, the x-axes of all of the panels will zoom together in the default state. If you desire the x-axes to be independently zoomed, click on "Unlock Zoom" in the "View" menu. This will unlock the x-axes and change the "Unlock Zoom" entry in the "View" menu to "Lock Zoom". Clicking on this new "Unlock Zoom" entry will restore the x-axis locked behavior.

    Deriving new nodes:

    NST allows the user to derive nodes based on arithmetic expressions of existing waveforms. For example, one might be interesting in displaying the difference between two signals. Note that derived nodes only operate on the most recently loaded file.

    In order to derive a new node, go to the "Derive" menu and then click on "New Derivation" in the pulldown menu. A popup window will then be generated with a entry box in which to type in the formula for the derived node. The syntax of this formula is as follows: 

    		<derived_node> = <node|scalar> <operation> <node|scalar>
				 [<operation> <node|scalar>] ...
	or
		<derived_node> = d/dx <node>

    where node is the node name for any plottable node in the circuit and operation is any one of +, -, *, /. Spaces need only be used for disambiguation. If you have a waveform named "2" and also want to use the number 2 as a scalar, for example, use "2.0" for the scalar to disambiguate it from the waveform.

    For example, to derive a node called "diff" that is the difference of the nodes "net_1" and "in", use the formula: 

    		diff = net_1 - in

    or if you want to display the mid-supply line, use: 

    		vdd2 = vdd/2.0

    Note that all NST formuli are case sensitive.

    Derivations can even be composed of other derivations.

    There are some other special functions that can be used in derivations like abs, log, sqrt. The syntax for these is: 

    		<function>( <vector|expression> )

    Note that there needs to be a space between the parentheses and the arguments but NO space between the function and the open paranthesis.

    Another set of functions returns a single value (or scalar): min, max, sum, mean, medium. You can convert these back to vectors by multiplying them by a unit vector, for example: 

    		max = max( net_3 ) * net_3 / net_3

    It seems redundant, but that's life.

    The bottom line of the derived node window is used for status and error messages. A comprehensive set of error messages have been added to try to help in generating valid formuli.

    Commonly used derivations can also be added to the .nstrc file so you don't have to retype them everytime you run NST. This is done by adding them to the DERIVE vairable, e.g: 

    		set DERIVE ""
		lappend DERIVE "vdd2 = vdd/2.0"

    Once a node has been derived, it will be added to the "Derive" pulldown menu and, by clicking on the checkbutton, this node can be plotted and unplotted in any selected window.

    Computing Power:

    Often you want to compute how much power was dissipated in a circuit. If you have both the voltage and current waveforms, NST will compute the power by integrating the instantaneous product of the current and voltage waveforms over a given range. NST then divides this integration by the range or cycle time to get the average power. To compute power, use the "Compute Power" command in the "View" menu.

    To simplify inputting the range, NST will default to the range specified by the measure box (the box created by stroking with button-2). You can then modify the values if you desire. If there is no measure box, the range defaults to the same values that were inputted the last time "Compute Power" was run.

    Text Annotations:

    You can add text to a panel with the "Annotate..." command in the "View" menu. The text will be added to the current panel. You can then move the text by clicking and holding Button-2 over it. You can remove individual annotations with Shift-Button-2 over them or clear all annotations with the "Clear All Annotations" command in the "View" menu.

    Changing the X-Axis:

    By default, the x-axis in NST is time. Sometimes it is desirable to have a different x-axis such as in generating transfer characteristics for gates or devices. NST provides a mechanism for changing the x-axis through the node listbox.

    To change the x-axis, select the desired node for the x-axis and then hit the "X" Button in the node listbox. This node will then be the x-axis until changed again. Note that since NST favors the most recently loaded file, if you change the x-axis of a file other than the most recently loaded file, the x-axis label will not change and other unforseen results may occur(?)

    Printing:

    NST can generate a postscript output file for the various graph panels using the "Print" menu. The print pulldown menu allows you to either print to a file or to the default printer. In addition, using radiobuttons the format of the postscript can be selected to be either black/white, grey-scale, or color. Note that multi-panel graphs will not display properly on most viewers (e.g. ghostview, pageview) but will print properly.

Using NST remotely:

    In addition to the screen buttons and menus described above, a simple TCL-level interface has been provided for remote control of NST. We have used this interface to control NST remotely from a schematic entry tool to permit cross-probing of highlighted nets. All of these commands can be accessed using the "send" command from another TK application like SUE.

    NST has the following TCL entry points: 

       nst_load filename            loads in a .tr0 file into spicetool
   nst_plot filename node       plots the node from a loaded filename
   nst_unplot filename node     unplots the node from a loaded filename
   nst_erase_all                clears all graph screens
   nst_copy old new             moves data from old filename to new
   nst_reset                    clears all screens, unloads all data

    nst_copy can be used for storing the waveforms for old spice runs. In order to use it in this way, first issue the following command before reloading the spice output deck from a new simulation, for example: 

    	nst_copy foo.tr0 foo.tr0~

    and then load the new spice output file 

    	nst_load foo.tr0

    now old data can be plotted using the command 

    	nst_plot foo.tr0~ node

ASCII Columnated File Format:

    NST, by default assumes that all files are of HSPICE binary format. In order to tell it that you have an ASCII file, the word "ASCII" must be near the beginning of the first line in the file. The ASCII file format is: 

    first line:		Title/Comment (must include word "ASCII")
Second line:		list of whitespace separated columns names
Remaining lines:	columns of ASCII data corresponding to column names

    Note that this format is very similar to HSPICE's .mt0 format. In order to read a .mt0 file, you must delete the first line and add the word ASCII to the new first line. In addition, if the column name line is broken across multiple lines, it must be put back together onto one line. Note that NST will read the data lines correctly even if they are broken over multiple lines.

NST Known Bugs and Limitations:

    • NST cannot plot a waveform named "node".

    • NST won't highlight the legend of a waveform whose name includes a brackets (i.e. [ or ]). The waveform will turn white, but the legend won't turn reverse video.
